6	Large language models are increasingly deployed for zero-shot information extraction~\cite{li2023codeie,sainz2024gollie,wei2023zeroshot}, but when generating relation triples $(h, r, t)$, neither entity is guaranteed to carry a type consistent with the ontology's domain/range constraints for $r$.

\paragraph{Grammar-Constrained Decoding.}
XGrammar~\cite{dong2025xgrammar}, Outlines~\cite{willard2023outlines}, Guidance~\cite{guidance2023}, and LMQL~\cite{beurer-kellner2023lmql} have made grammar-constrained decoding the standard for structured LLM output, ensuring every token belongs to a grammar-valid continuation.
DOMINO~\cite{beurer-kellner2024domino} and ASAp~\cite{park2024grammar} further address distribution distortion, making grammar enforcement statistically principled.
However, these methods operate at the syntactic level---they ensure format validity but cannot enforce cross-field semantic constraints such as ontology domain/range rules.

\paragraph{Semantic Constrained Decoding for Code.}
In code generation, constrained decoding has been extended to enforce semantic properties: Synchromesh~\cite{synchromesh_iclr2022} enforces type and scope constraints via dynamic token masks; PICARD~\cite{scholak2021picard} performs incremental SQL parsing to reject type-invalid tokens; MGD~\cite{mgd_neurips2023} applies static-analysis monitors for type checking at decode time; and \citet{pldi2025_type_constrained_codegen} compile full type systems into prefix automata for logits masking.
These demonstrate that richer-than-CFG constraints are feasible at decode time, but exclusively in the code domain---OntoCoDec migrates this paradigm to information extraction.

\paragraph{Vocabulary and Type-Constrained Generation.}
\citet{roth_yih_2004} establish that relational type compatibility should be a hard constraint via integer linear programming, though applied post-hoc; see also~\cite{xie2016tkrl}.
GENRE~\cite{decao2021genre}, NeuroLogic~\cite{lu2021neurologic}, AdaKGC~\cite{adakgc_emnlp2023}, GCD~\cite{geng2023gcd}, and GoLLIE~\cite{sainz2024gollie} constrain \emph{which tokens} can appear (vocabulary membership) but not \emph{which type combinations} are valid for a given relation---OntoCoDec enforces relational constraints where the valid set depends on the relation type generated earlier in the same sequence.

\paragraph{Structural Constraints via Training.}
TANL~\cite{paolini2021tanl}, REBEL~\cite{cabot2021rebel}, UIE~\cite{lu2022uie}, GoLLIE~\cite{sainz2024gollie}, KnowCoder~\cite{knowcoder_acl2024}, and CodeIE~\cite{li2023codeie} encode IE structure through training or schema-as-code prompting.
These provide \emph{soft} guidance---the model learns to prefer valid outputs but cannot guarantee compliance, as shown by non-trivial violation rates even in fine-tuned systems.
OntoCoDec provides complementary \emph{hard} enforcement that is training-free and composable with these methods.

\paragraph{Post-hoc Ontology Validation.}
ODKE+~\cite{khorshidi2025odke} uses ontology snippets as prompt context; OntoGPT~\cite{spires_2024} validates outputs against ontologies in a second pass; OntoLogX~\cite{ontologx_2025} applies SHACL validation with iterative re-prompting, reducing violations by ${\sim}10\times$ across correction rounds.
These detect-then-fix approaches waste compute on violated outputs, whereas OntoCoDec \emph{prevents} violations during decoding by redirecting probability mass to valid alternatives.

\paragraph{Quality Impact of Constrained Decoding.}
CRANE~\cite{banerjee2025crane} shows grammar restrictions suppress chain-of-thought reasoning, \citet{schall2025hiddencost} find 10--30\% degradation on reasoning tasks, and \citet{tam2024letmespeak} demonstrate that format constraints harm reasoning benchmarks.
However, \citet{tam2024letmespeak}'s results also show extraction-style tasks are robust to---or benefit from---constraints, and IE is fundamentally extraction rather than reasoning.
OntoCoDec confirms this: violations decrease by 94\% on SciERC with zero F1 degradation, as constraints target only type tokens while leaving entity spans unconstrained.

\medskip
\noindent
OntoCoDec is the first system to automatically compile IE ontology domain/range constraints into token-level semantic masks, extending grammar-constrained decoding from syntactic to semantic enforcement for information extraction (extended survey in Appendix~\ref{app:related_work}).

\paragraph{CF Severity.}
% exp_ids: phase2_scierc_full_s1 (CF=9.90%), phase2_scierc_grammar_only (CF=0.08%),

DR violations produce ontologically invalid triples---a hard constraint failure that no downstream system can recover from.
CF violations are qualitatively different: each individual triple remains type-valid with respect to its own relation's domain/range rules; only cross-triple consistency is broken when the same entity receives different types across relations.
The dominant conflict pattern---\emph{Generic}$\leftrightarrow$\emph{OtherScientificTerm} (85 of 245 affected entities on SciERC; Table~\ref{tab:cf-distribution})---reflects genuine semantic ambiguity in the type system rather than a systematic method failure; conflicts involving \textsc{Generic} account for 63.3\% of all CF violations.
Ablation cleanly attributes CF to the semantic layer: grammar-only decoding yields CF\,=\,0.08\%, matching the unconstrained baseline, while the full system reaches 9.90\% on SciERC and 2.57\% on DocRED (Qwen3-8B; 12.02\% DocRED for Llama-3.1-8B), confirming that CF arises from per-relation independent enforcement where each relation's constraint mask is computed without access to type decisions made for other relations (extended analysis in Appendix~\ref{app:discussion}).
% exp_ids: phase2_scierc_grammar_only, phase2_docred_full_s1, llama_docred_full_s1

\paragraph{Dataset-Dependent F1 Impact.}
% exp_ids: d012_bootstrap_ci (DocRED +0.50pp p<0.001, SciERC +0.13pp p=0.58),
%          phase0_docred_unconstrained (RV=29.66%), phase0_scierc_unconstrained (RV=1.39%)
The divergence in F1 significance between DocRED ($+$0.50\,pp, $p < 0.001$) and SciERC ($+$0.13\,pp, $p = 0.58$) traces to a single mechanism: grammar-layer elimination of out-of-vocabulary relation names.
DocRED's baseline RV of 29.66\% produces 5{,}189 OOV predictions counted as false positives; eliminating them yields a significant precision gain.
SciERC's baseline RV is only 1.39\% (24 OOV predictions), too few to produce a detectable F1 effect.
Llama-3.1-8B's lower baseline RV (16.03\%) yields a smaller but directionally consistent improvement ($+$0.29\,pp vs.\ $+$0.50\,pp), confirming that F1 gain magnitude is proportional to baseline OOV rate.

% exp_ids: phase2_scierc_full_s1, phase2_docred_full_s1, llama_docred_full_s1
